The Numbers Room · a room with two darks it can never reach

The Quiet Room

Twenty-five brass lamps. Tap one and it flips itself and its four neighbours — leave the whole panel dark to win. Each lamp is a bit, each board a vector over GF(2), and a press just adds a column of the toggle matrix — so order never matters and pressing twice undoes itself. Solving is one clean linear system, no search. But two patterns live in the matrix's kernel: press every lamp of either and the room does not change at all. They are the only two moves the lamps can never see — and they make 2²³ of the 2²⁵ boards solvable, the rest provably impossible.

Kernel dimension: 2 · so 2²³ of 2²⁵ patterns are solvable, the rest provably impossible.
The lamps are a vector space over GF(2), and pressing is linear — so the boards you can ever reach are exactly the column space of the toggle matrix, and a board is solvable iff it is orthogonal to that matrix's left-nullspace. That nullspace — the kernel — has dimension two here: two quiet patterns the lamps can never change, and every solvable board has exactly four solutions that differ by them. Hand-paint a lamp and the provenance meter goes red though the board may still be reachable; deal a lone lit lamp and no press-set exists at all.  ·  Back to the Numbers Room
